load_menu.name: Load Menu

pack.help:
v%s by %s

Reset every value of profile '%s' to the defaults?
Click again within %d seconds to reset
reset.done: Profile '%s' is back to the defaults

settings.name: Settings

short_name.name: Short Name

user_separator.name: Separator: %s

errors.name: Errors Always In Stand

warn.name: Warning

error.name: Error

success.name: Success

all.name: All At Once

newline.name: Text On A New Line

icon.name: Icon: %s

general.name: General

night_start.name: Night Starts At

background_night.name: Night Background Color

flash_color_night.name: Night Flash Color

stop_on_change.name: Stop After Changes

stop_on_change.stopped: %s changed on disk: the script stops, start it again

updater_log_both_ways.name: Write Both Ways

Rename the script '%s' to '%s'?

Stand profile states saved under the old name won't apply to the new one.
rename.invalid: '%s' isn't a valid name: use letters, digits and _
rename.busy: Not renamed: an open folder is keeping the script from being renamed (%s). Close Explorer windows, editors and consoles open inside it and try again

list.name: Language

language.name: Language: %s

auto.name: Auto (Stand)
auto.help: Show the script in Stand's language

language.unavailable: Stand is in English, so the script can't be shown in another language: it follows Stand. The choice is kept and works while Stand is in another language

create.name: Create Translation

code.name: Language Code

loop.name: Loop

by_name.help: Calls a function (written with brackets: util.toast()), or reads a table (opened with {} at the end) or a variable, by the name typed here, with arguments

function.name: Function Name
function.help: A path with dots. Stand's tables: util.toast, entities.get_user_vehicle_as_handle. The script's: game.repair_vehicle; its tables named like Stand's are reached with Atdar in front: Atdar.util.hash. The first part may be a module's name: VehicleManager.get. With a colon the function is called as a method: VehicleManager:get. A name alone finds the function, the script's natives too: set_explosive_melee_this_frame. A function is called only when written with brackets: util.toast(); without them it is only read. A table is opened in the Value list only when written with {} at the end: Atdar.util{}; without them it is only looked at: its nested tables are lists, but its functions can't be called and its values can't be typed over. In the brackets #1, #2 are the values of the argument fields: util.toast(#1), util.toast(tostring(#1)). asstr(#1): the argument as text; asint(#1): as a whole number; allasstr(): all the arguments as text, with a notice of them; astext and allastext call nothing and only show the name and the arguments

delete.help: Deletes this file. Click twice within 5 seconds

add_line.name: Add Line
add_line.help: Type a line of code: it's added at the end of the file

insert_line.name: Insert Line
insert_line.help: Number, a colon and the code: 3: local x = 1 puts it before line 3

remove_line.name: Remove Line
remove_line.help: Type the number of the line to take away

code.mistake: %s.pluto saved, but the code has a mistake: %s

errors.name: A file name has letters, digits and _ only
errors.exists: There's a file with this name already
errors.main: The main file can't be deleted
errors.insert: Type it as number: code (3: local x = 1)

pick.name: Pick Function
pick.help: Takes the function's name from a list, so it needn't be typed: your short names, the registry, or a module's functions

registry.name: Registry
registry.help: The short names shipped with the script (core/call_function/short_name.json)

modules.name: Modules
modules.help: A module's functions, called as its methods (Module:function)

history.name: History
history.help: The last 10 calls with what was typed for them. A click calls one again. Kept until the game is closed

repeat_last.name: Repeat Last
repeat_last.help: Calls the latest call again with the same arguments

copy_result.name: Copy Result
copy_result.help: Puts what the function gave, whole, in the clipboard
copy_result.unavailable: This Stand has no clipboard function

log_result.name: Log Result
log_result.help: Writes what the function gave, whole, to the log

open_logs.name: Open Logs In Editor
open_logs.help: Shows the log files in the Files Editor

open_short_names.name: Open Short Names In Editor
open_short_names.help: Shows user/call_function/short_names.json in the Files Editor

short_names.name: Use Short Names
short_names.help: The functions in the list are named by the last part of the path: PLAYER_PED_ID, not PLAYER.PLAYER_PED_ID; toast, not util.toast. A short name can also be typed in Function Name and Add: the entry from store/<script>/user/call_function/short_names.json is used first (for example, {"ped": "PLAYER.PLAYER_PED_ID"}); otherwise the first matching function is used, first in the script and then in Stand's tables. Off: the full path.
short_names.many: %s: %d functions have this name, the first is used

hide_function.name: Hide Function Word
hide_function.help: A function in a table's list is written (amount): void instead of function(amount): void. The lists made after the change follow

registry.bad_param: %s (short_name.json): parameter %d has no "name", so the registry's parameters for it are left out
registry.no_path: short_name.json: "%s" is left out, it has no "path" (a text)

show_time.name: Disable Call Time For All
show_time.help: On: no loop shows how long its calls take, whatever the Show Call Time of each function says. Off: each function's own Show Call Time decides. In the loops of Call Function and of a module's functions

show_result.name: Disable Result On Screen For All
show_result.help: On: no loop draws what its function gave, whatever the Show Result On Screen of each function says. Off: each function's own Show Result On Screen decides. In the loops of Call Function and of a module's functions

result_length.name: Result Length On Screen
result_length.help: How many characters of the result are drawn on the screen; the rest is cut off with ... A long table doesn't run off the screen

functions.name: Functions
functions.help: Functions kept in a list, each with a field for every argument. Add puts one in, Clear takes one out by its number

add.name: Add
add.help: Type the path of a function to put it in the list: game.repair_vehicle, PLAYER.PLAYER_PED_ID. One that takes arguments gets a field for each of them, one that takes none is a button
add.args_dropped: %s: the arguments in the brackets are not kept, type them in the fields of the function

clear.name: Clear
clear.help: Type the number of a function (it's before the name) to take it out of the list; the others are numbered again

clear_all.name: Clear All
clear_all.help: Takes every function out of the list
clear_all.done: The list of functions is cleared

save.name: Save Functions
save.help: Keeps the list of functions in a file, store/<script>/user/call_function/saved_functions.json, and puts it back at the next start. The paths only, not what's typed in the fields. Off: the file stays, it just isn't used

guide.name: Arguments Guide
guide.help: Sends to Stand how to write the functions' arguments in the argument fields
guide.text: Each argument has its own field, by the type written for it in the code. Where an expression is taken it's worked out as in Lua: 5, true, "text", v3.new(1, 2, 3), entities.get_user_vehicle_as_handle(). A word without quotes is text: a call is always written with its brackets, user_ped(). Worked out at each call. An empty field is not given; a parameter written without ? and with no default must be given. A vector is a list: the whole vector, then x, y and z that can be typed over. In Function Name a function is called only when written with brackets, util.toast(); a table is opened as a list when written with {} at the end, util{} (its tables are lists, its functions can be called, its values typed over), without {} it is only looked at (its functions can't be called, its values can't be typed over); one item by its key in brackets: util.list[1], util["name"]. #1, #2 in the brackets of Function Name are the argument fields: util.toast(tostring(#1))

added.help: A field for each argument by the type the code says, then Call, Call After, Loop...
added.table_help: Opens the table: what is in it is a list, a value is a field to type a new one, a function is a list to call
added.button_help: Calls the function; a table or a variable is read. What it gives is in the notice

call.name: Call
call.help: Calls a function once, reads a table or a variable; the result is in the notice, in the Variable line and, for a table, in the Value list. With a number of milliseconds picked (Left / Right) it is called after that long, not at once

call_function.template_no_fields: #1, #2 point to the argument fields, and this function has none: write the arguments in its brackets
call_function.bad_ref: #%d: there is no such argument (the function has %d)
call_function.braces_on_function: %s is a function: {} is not needed, it is called with brackets
call_function.brackets_on_table: %s is a table: brackets are only for functions, a table is opened with {} at the end
call_function.file_bad: %s: the file is damaged or is not a JSON object, it is read as empty
call_function.short_names_bad: %s: "%s" is left out, the name and the path must both be texts

stand_api.bad_entry: stand_api.json: "%s" is not an object with a list of "params", it is not used

call_function.command_unknown: command.json: "%s" is not a command of the script (known: %s)
call_function.command_names: command.json: the names of "%s" must be a list of texts
call_function.command_duplicate: command.json: the name "%s" is used by "%s" and by "%s", the first one is used
call_function.unclosed: a bracket or a quote is not closed

pointer_editor.name: Pointer Editor
pointer_editor.help: Places in the game's memory that are found by a signature (a pattern of bytes). The ones made here are kept and stored again at every start
pointer_editor.not_own: Stored by the script itself: it can be scanned, not changed here

add.name: Add Pointer
add.help: name = pattern, for example roll = 48 8B ?? ?? 89. The pattern is bytes in hex with a space between, ?? is any byte

read.name: Read Bytes
read.help: An address (0x7FF...) or the name of a found pointer, and how many bytes after a comma: roll, 16. The bytes are written as a pattern

read_value.name: Read Value
read_value.help: The int at an address or a found pointer plus an offset, as: ped_factory, 0x8. The offset is hex (0x8) or decimal and can be left out

chain.name: Pointer Chain
chain.help: Follows pointers: ped_factory, 0x8, 0x10A0, 0x280. The first is a name or an address, then offsets; all but the last are hops, the last is read as an int

copy_code.name: Copy Code
copy_code.help: Puts the code that finds this pointer in the clipboard
copy_code.unavailable: This Stand has no clipboard function: the code is in the log

guide.name: Instruction
guide.help: How to use the editor, step by step, with ped_factory as the example: each topic sends a message
guide.item_help: Sends the message with the example

add.name: Add Pointer
add.text: Type in the Add Pointer field: ped_factory = 48 8B 05 ? ? ? ? 48 83 78 08 00 74 EB 48 8B 0D. A name, an equals sign, then the pattern (bytes in hex, ? is any byte)

setup.name: Set Up The Pointer
setup.text: Open ped_factory > Settings: Kind = rip, At = 3, Size = 4, Extra = 0. Kind says what the pointer gives, At is where the number is in the pattern

scan.name: Scan
scan.text: Press Scan in ped_factory: the rip section shows the address of the CPedFactory variable, the address section shows where the pattern was found

bytes.name: Read Bytes
bytes.text: In Read Bytes type: ped_factory, 16. It gives 16 bytes at the found address, written as a pattern

value.name: Read Value
value.text: In Read Value type: ped_factory, 0x8. It gives the int at the found address plus 0x8. The offset is optional (0x.. or decimal)

chain.name: Pointer Chain
chain.text: In Pointer Chain type: ped_factory, 0x8, 0x10A0, 0x280. The first is a name or an address, then the offsets: all but the last are hops (a pointer is read there), the last is read as an int

code.name: Copy Code
code.text: At the end of a pointer's page press Copy Code: the line pointers.store(...) with its settings goes to the clipboard, ready for the code

pointer.help: A pointer: open it to scan it and to see or change how it is found

settings.name: Settings
settings.help: How the pointer is found: the pattern, what is taken from the place found, and Remove

delete_one.name: Delete Result
delete_one.help: Takes the last result away: the one before it is the last then

delete_all.name: Delete Results Above
delete_all.help: Takes all the results above away, the last one and the ones before it. The numbers start again

delete_past.name: Delete Past Results
delete_past.help: Takes the results before the last one away; the last one stays

scan.name: Scan
scan.help: Searches the pattern in the game's memory now

pattern.name: Pattern
pattern.help: Bytes in hex with a space between, ?? or ? for any byte: 48 8B ?? ?? 89

kind.name: Kind
kind.help: What is taken from the place found: address (where it is), rip (where a call or lea there points), offset (a number in the instruction)

at.name: At
at.help: Bytes from the start of the pattern to the number (rip, offset)

size.name: Size
size.help: The number is 4 bytes (default) or 1 byte (offset)

extra.name: Extra
extra.help: Bytes that follow the number in the instruction (rip)

remove.name: Remove
remove.help: Takes this pointer away. Click twice within 5 seconds

errors.name: A name has letters, digits and _, and starts with a letter
errors.pattern: A pattern is bytes in hex with a space between (48 8B), ?? is any byte
errors.exists: There is a pointer with this name already
errors.missing: There is no such pointer here
errors.kind: A kind is address, rip or offset
errors.number: A number, 0 or more, is needed
errors.bytes: That is not an address, nor a pointer that is found
errors.bad_spec: Type it as: name or address, then offsets (ped_factory, 0x8, 0x280)
errors.not_found: The first one is not an address, nor a pointer that is found
errors.bad_pointer: Step %d: there is no readable pointer there

delete_script.name: Delete Script
delete_script.help: Deletes the script from Stand's Lua Scripts. Opens a list with the confirm button
delete_script.warning:
Delete the script '%s' with all its files, profiles and settings too (launcher, lib, store and resources folders)?
This can't be undone.
delete_script.done: Script '%s' deleted (%d file(s)). It stops now

keep.name: Keep Profiles And Settings
keep.help: Keeps store/<name>/profiles and config.json, so a reinstall finds them

confirm.name: Delete Script For Good
confirm.help: Click twice within 5 seconds: deletes the launcher and the lib, store and resources folders, then stops the script
confirm.again_notice: Click it again within %d seconds to delete

delete_script.warning_keep:
Delete the script '%s' (launcher, lib, store and resources folders)? Profiles and settings are kept.
This can't be undone.

clear_feed.name: Remove Game Notifications
clear_feed.help: Takes every notification of the script out of the game's feed; the game's and other scripts' stay
clear_feed.done: Notifications taken out of the feed: %d
clear_feed.none: No notifications of the script in the feed

updater_menu.name: Update
updater_menu.help: Checking for and installing a new version of the script

changes.name: Changes
changes.help: Shows what the available version changes
changes.none: No changes to show: nothing to update, or updates weren't checked yet

on_start.name: Check On Start
on_start.help: Checks for a new version every time the script starts. Not while Check For Updates Every is 0

check.name: Check For Updates
check.help: Finds out whether a new version of the script is out

install.name: Update
install.help: Downloads and installs the new version; profiles and settings stay

before.name: Check Before Updating
before.help: Update checks for a newer version first, and does nothing if there is none

progress_notify.name: Progress In Notifications
progress_notify.help: Tells how far the download of an update has come, every 10%

auto.name: Update Automatically
auto.help: Installs a new version by itself as soon as a check finds one

check_days.name: Check For Updates Every (Days)
check_days.help: How often to check whether a new version is out. Applied on a click; 0 - never
check_days.set: Updates will be checked every %d days

version.name: Update To Version
version.help: Installs a version, an older one too: type it, or pick one of the releases below. The script restarts; profiles and settings stay

input.name: Version
input.help: A version (0.1.8: the release tagged v0.1.8), or a tag, a branch or a commit of the repo. Installed when typed

sync.name: Sync With Branch
sync.help: On: the list below is the releases of the Branch picked above. Off: the releases of every branch, each marked with its branch (0.1.11: main). Installs nothing

limit.name: Limit Shown To
limit.help: How many of the newest versions the list below shows

version.item_help: Installs this version, then the script restarts
version.warning: Install version %s? The script's files are replaced and it restarts; profiles and settings stay

branch.name: Branch: %s
branch.help: Where updates come from: main - tried versions, experiment - the newest, less tried
branch.set: Updates will come from the %s branch

msg.busy: A check or an update is already running
msg.no_access: the script has no internet access (turn off Disable Internet Access in Stand > Lua Scripts > %s)
msg.up_to_date: The script is up to date (version %s)
msg.found: Version %s is out: %d file(s) to change. Press Update to install it
msg.installed: Updated to version %s. The script restarts
msg.stale: The new version is still reaching GitHub's servers, so the downloaded files don't match yet. Nothing was changed. Wait a few minutes, press Check, then Update again
